reading: Three walls, and the same new cable put into each. Timber frame, as in most new US homes: pulled through holes drilled in the studs, behind the board; quick. Plastered brick, as in most German homes, repainted: a duct screwed onto the surface and painted over; quick, but it stays on show. Plastered brick, renovated: a channel cut, the cable laid and plastered over; slow, and the channel stays as a scar.
sourceNote: No numbers are drawn; no hours or days are given. 'Most new US homes': 94% of new single-family homes completed in 2025 had wood frames (NAHB-2026, from the Census Survey of Construction). 'Most German homes': about two in three new homes approved in 2020 were of masonry (DESTATIS-2021); hidden cables in masonry run in fixed installation zones, in channels cut and plastered (BAUNETZ-DIN18015). The rest describes general building practice; the analogy is the owner's (transcript 2026-11-16-020).
